record.paper_title: Open Questions in CMR Manganites, Relevance of Clustered States, and Analogies with other Compounds
record.original_question: Can cuprates exhibit colossal or other percolative competition-driven effects analogous to manganites because small superconducting, antiferromagnetic, or charge-ordered regions coexist and can be aligned by weak perturbations, and what is the actual order of the antiferromagnet–superconductor transition in clean cuprates: first-order, bicritical, tricritical, or tetracritical?

evidence.quote: Could it be that "colossal" effects occur in cuprates and other materials as well?

Even at a phenomenological level, the order of the transition between an antiferromagnet and a superconductor is still unknown. ... More work is needed to clarify this elementary aspect of the problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider hole-doped cuprate compounds, modeled as a strongly correlated electron system on a two-dimensional CuO2 lattice in which several types of order may coexist locally: d-wave superconductivity (SC), antiferromagnetism (AF), and charge order (e.g. stripes or checkerboards). Suppose that, as in a phase-separated landscape, the system in some doping range supports nanoscale clusters of distinct competing orders that can be reoriented or grown by weak external perturbations (small magnetic, electric, or strain fields).

(a) Determine whether such a clean cuprate system can exhibit "colossal" responses analogous to the colossal magnetoresistance observed in manganites, i.e. whether weak perturbations can align or percolate the competing nanoscale clusters so as to produce dramatic (orders-of-magnitude) changes in transport, magnetic, or superconducting properties. Provide either (i) a microscopic mechanism and quantitative estimate showing under what conditions such percolative colossal effects can occur in cuprates, or (ii) an argument ruling them out.

(b) For an idealized clean cuprate (without quenched disorder) at zero temperature, determine the nature of the quantum phase transition between the antiferromagnetic insulating phase and the d-wave superconducting phase as a function of hole doping. Specifically, decide which of the following scenarios is realized in the global phase diagram (in the temperature–doping plane):
   1. a single direct first-order transition,
   2. a bicritical point at finite temperature where two second-order lines merge tangentially into a first-order line,
   3. a tricritical point at which a line of second-order transitions becomes first-order, or
   4. a tetracritical point at which an intermediate coexistence (AF + SC) phase is bounded by two distinct second-order lines.
artifact.category_tag: strongly correlated electrons and competing orders in cuprates
artifact.status_search_result: The questions remain open. The order of the AF–SC transition in clean cuprates is still debated: SO(5) and related theoretical analyses predict a bicritical point for repulsive biquadratic AF–SC couplings and a tetracritical (biconical) point for attractive ones, with no consensus from experiment in clean systems. Recent work (e.g. 2023 Nature Communications on disorder-removed lightly-doped cuprates) and 2022 analyses of bi/tetracritical phase diagrams continue to investigate the issue without a definitive resolution. Whether percolative "colossal" effects analogous to manganites occur in cuprates is also still an open phenomenological question.

status_evidence.title: Bi- and tetracritical phase diagrams in three dimensions
status_evidence.snippet: Two ordered phases are separated by a first-order line meeting at a bicritical point, or by an intermediate mixed phase bounded by two critical lines meeting at a tetracritical point.
status_evidence.claim: The bicritical-vs-tetracritical question for competing orders is still being analyzed theoretically as of 2022.

status_evidence.title: Unveiling phase diagram of the lightly doped high-Tc cuprate superconductors with disorder removed
status_evidence.snippet: Phase diagram of clean lightly-doped cuprates is being mapped experimentally.
status_evidence.claim: The clean-limit AF–SC phase diagram of cuprates is still the subject of ongoing experimental investigation.

status_evidence.title: Bicritical and Tetracritical Phenomena and Scaling Properties of the SO(5) Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Bicritical point is stable to biquadratic perturbations of AF–SC repulsions, while the biconical tetracritical point takes its place for attractive interactions.
status_evidence.claim: Theory predicts either bicritical or tetracritical behavior depending on microscopic parameters; which is realized in cuprates is unsettled.
